description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Provides types supporting the reading and writing of Internet messages, including:
- RFC 5322 and RFC 6532: a streaming reader of the header fields of a message, with UTF-8 in field bodies
- RFC 2045 and RFC 2046: a streaming reader of the MIME entities of a message, with multipart bodies, embedded messages and transfer decoding
- RFC 5322, RFC 6532, RFC 2045 and RFC 2046: streaming writers of header fields and MIME entities, with folding, transfer encoding, multipart boundaries and byte-exact copying of what has not changed
- RFC 5322, RFC 6532 and RFC 6854: typed addresses, mailboxes, groups, message identifiers and keyword phrases, parsed from the modern and obsolete syntax and written in the modern form where the modern syntax can express them
- RFC 5322: typed date-times, parsed from the modern and obsolete syntax and written in the modern form, which keep an unknown UTC offset (-0000), a leap second and whether a day of the week was given
- RFC 2047: encoded words in display names, keyword phrases, comments and unstructured fields, decoded when read and written where text is not US-ASCII
- RFC 2045, RFC 2183, RFC 2231, RFC 2392 and RFC 3282: the MIME-Version, Content-Type, Content-Transfer-Encoding, Content-ID, Content-Description, Content-Disposition and Content-Language header fields, with cid: URIs
- RFC 5322 and RFC 6854: a message object model with typed accessors for the origination, destination, identification, informational, resent and trace fields, a reader and writer that keep unchanged fields byte for byte, and the conformance checks of RFC 5322 §3.6
- RFC 2045, RFC 2046, RFC 2387 and RFC 2392: a MIME entity tree with decoded content, text and HTML bodies, attachments, cid: lookup, a message builder, and a writer that rewrites only what has changed
- RFC 2557 and RFC 2387: MHTML files, with Content-Location, the root of a multipart/related entity, URLs resolved to their parts, a document builder, and a reader and writer
- RFC 4155: mbox files in the mboxrd, mboxo, mboxcl and mboxcl2 variants, with a reader that takes one message at a time, so a mailbox of any size can be processed, and a writer
- Apple Mail EMLX files: a message with its byte count and its property list of metadata, with typed flags and dates, unknown keys kept, partial files with their parts supplied by the caller, and a reader and writer
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes:
- `MboxWriter` no longer reports a message that can't be read back with its options as `LongBodyLine`; the reader's error is thrown with its own kind, position and entity path.
- `ImfReader`, `ImfEntityReader`, `MboxReader`, `EmlxReader` and `MhtmlReader` reject a line in a multipart entity that starts with its boundary and is not a delimiter, including the delimiters of a nested multipart entity whose boundary starts with the outer one, as `ImfWriter` already does (RFC 2046 §5.1.1).
- A parameter given both as `name` and in an RFC 2231 form such as `name*` is now rejected as a duplicate (RFC 6838 §4.3), where the RFC 2231 value used to be kept.
- Writers throw an ImfFileException for a multipart entity that was read with no close delimiter and hasn't changed, unless their options set AllowMissingBoundaryTerminator; ImfMessage.Validate reports it as InvalidBodyStructure.
- `ImfEntity.GetText` throws `ImfFileException` for a `text/html`, `text/xml`, `text/xml-external-parsed-entity` or `text/markdown` entity with no `charset` parameter, instead of decoding it as US-ASCII. These types have no default character set (RFC 6657 §3), so read `GetContent` and find it as the format says.
- `ImfEntity.GetText` throws `ImfFileException` for a `text` entity with the `+xml` suffix, such as `text/foo+xml`, and no `charset` parameter, instead of decoding it as US-ASCII. These types have no default character set (RFC 7303 §4.2), so read `GetContent` and find it as XML says.

Fixed:
- The package now includes its XML documentation, so IntelliSense shows member descriptions.
- VCard FLOAT and EMLX real values are read as the same double on .NET Framework as on .NET 10, including negative zero.
- `EmlxWriter`, `MboxWriter`, and `ImfWriter` writing a message from an mbox file no longer alter the bytes of a body they would have labelled `binary` under `AllowBinaryTransferEncoding`; such a body is now encoded instead.
- `ImfWriter`, `MboxWriter` and `EmlxWriter` writing a message that holds a message read from a file with other line breaks, such as one from an mbox or EMLX file being forwarded, now change its line breaks to those of the output, instead of refusing it or writing bare LF line breaks into a CRLF message.
- `ImfWriter`, `MboxWriter`, `EmlxWriter`, `ImfEntityWriter` and `ImfHeaderWriter` now write a header field read from a file with other line breaks, such as one from an mbox file added to a message read from an `.eml` file, with the line breaks of the message, instead of writing bare LF line breaks into a CRLF message.
- RFC 6533 message/global-headers, -delivery-status and -disposition-notification entities may be quoted-printable or base64.
- A new UTF-8 header field no longer makes ImfMessage.Body, Validate or a Utf8 writer fail.
- MboxReader no longer adds a stray line feed to the start of a message read after skipping part of a CRLF message.
- ImfWriter adds MIME-Version to a message after a part of a multipart read without it changes.
- MboxReader applies the line-length limit to quoted From lines correctly after 8-bit and CRLF lines.
- MboxReader counts a carriage return that ends the file as part of a quoted From line.
- Header text decoding (`ImfHeaderText`) decodes "Q"-encoded words with lower-case hexadecimal digits, such as `=?UTF-8?Q?=c3=a9?=`, by default, which RFC 2047 §4.2 allows; before, they were decoded only with `ImfOptions.AllowMalformedEncodedWords`.
- Quoted parameter values accept the US-ASCII control characters that RFC 822 allows, as text or as quoted-pairs, instead of rejecting them.
- Content-Type and Content-Disposition fields accept a quoted-pair whose backslash ends a folded line, such as `filename="a\<CRLF> b"`, and read it as the space after the fold (RFC 5322 §2.2.3); before, the field was rejected.
- EmlxPlistValue.TryGetDouble gives the nearest double for a hexadecimal integer too large for a long.
- `EmlxWriter`, `MboxWriter`, `MhtmlWriter`, and `ImfWriter` writing a message from an mbox file no longer alter the CR and LF octets of a body that isn't text and that they would have labelled `7bit` or `8bit`; such a body is now encoded instead, and one that asks for `7bit` or `8bit` is refused.
- Writers refuse a moved part or separately read message whose kept bytes hold a delimiter of a boundary around it.
- A refusal of an entity inside a held message with other line breaks, such as one read from an mbox file, gives the `EntityPath` of that entity within the message being written, not within the held message.
- The refusal of a `binary` entity, or one with an extension mechanism, whose line breaks would change gives its `EntityPath`.

Changed:
- A `text/*` body from a forward-only stream, written as quoted-printable, has its bare LFs encoded as `=0A` instead of written as CRLF line breaks, so the content is kept as it is (RFC 2045 §6.7 rule 4).
